claims.claim: Arista sits on the AI-infrastructure interconnect bottleneck: larger accelerator clusters increase bandwidth, latency, power-density and cooling pressure, supporting demand for high-speed Ethernet fabrics, optics and network operating software.

Its structural resilience comes from an open multi-vendor silicon/optics ecosystem plus EOS/software breadth, but the causal thesis depends on Ethernet retaining meaningful share against proprietary fabrics and customer-designed alternatives.

factors.name: bottleneckControl
factors.basis: 1.6T switching, high-density optics and EOS address bandwidth/power/cooling constraints in AI clusters.

factors.name: substitutionResilience
factors.basis: Open Ethernet ecosystem reduces lock-in concerns but proprietary interconnects and customer designs remain credible substitutes.

factors.name: scenarioRobustness
factors.basis: Cloud AI, conventional data center, campus and branch/security surfaces diversify deployment paths.

causalEdges.from: accelerator cluster scale and bandwidth intensity
causalEdges.mechanism: larger clusters require more high-throughput low-latency interconnect while power/cooling constraints reward efficient networking
causalEdges.falsifier: AI architectures materially reduce merchant Ethernet demand or proprietary fabrics dominate incremental deployments

causalEdges.mechanism: interoperability and operating consistency broaden customer adoption paths
causalEdges.falsifier: 1.6T/XPO adoption remains narrow or customers standardize on incompatible alternatives

risks.risk: Several next-generation products still require qualification and scaled post-launch adoption.

unknowns.unknown: Long-run scale-up Ethernet share and economics versus proprietary fabrics remain unsettled.

claims.claim: Current execution is not merely narrative: Q2 2026 exceeded $3B revenue and named hyperscaler validation exists, but that does not prove the economics of the newest 1.6T/XPO products before scaled availability and adoption.

The principal red-team pressure is concentration plus architecture substitution: a small set of very large cloud buyers can change deployment timing or favor proprietary/customer-designed interconnects.

factors.name: financialOperatingMomentum
factors.basis: Record quarterly revenue supports present execution rather than roadmap-only claims.

factors.name: substitutionResilience
factors.basis: Ethernet is credible but faces proprietary and customer-designed alternatives.

factors.name: pricingPower
factors.basis: Reviewed evidence does not isolate AI-fabric product pricing or margins.

causalEdges.from: named hyperscaler validation and product availability
causalEdges.mechanism: qualification must convert into scaled deployments
causalEdges.falsifier: availability slips, customers do not scale deployments, or competing architectures take incremental share

risks.risk: Customer concentration amplifies volatility if a major cloud buyer changes architecture, timing or procurement strategy.
1.6T/liquid-cooled products carry execution, component/optics supply and qualification risk.
Strong current growth raises the execution bar and can magnify disappointment if AI capex or share gains slow.

contradictions.claim: Strong current execution versus still-forward next-generation economics
contradictions.resolution: Both are true: existing scale is evidenced, while new-platform adoption economics remain future evidence.

unknowns.unknown: Exact AI-networking revenue/margin contribution and security-level valuation are not established here.
